title: Kotodama: a new grammar game from scratch
question: This is a playable prototype, not pictures: play it at https://fumbleforce.github.io/tower-of-words/game3d/minigames/kotodama.html (phone or desktop, about four minutes). It's a new game, started over after "even less fun, start over, write a new game from scratch, make it the most fun and impressive grammar game in existence". Is this fun? Round 2 (after your note: translations cut off, too casual, instructions unclear): the first twelve pictures show the fixes. Same game; the translations fit at every size, people speak politely (～さん, ください, です/ます; the machines still get plain だして), and the first command is a three-step walkthrough with a hand. Round 3 (after "kotodama: fun, keep going with it"; tapping over dragging, better machines): the first seven pictures. Same game. The vending machine, hot-water pot and fridge are redrawn with idle motion and a dispense, and the drinks are redrawn to match. Every action was already a tap; now a unit test keeps it that way, and the particle buttons pulse while a word waits for its particle.

media.caption: Round 3, before: the machines and drinks as they were (SVG, shown large and at phone size).

Round 3, after: a red street vending machine (lit COLD sign, two shelves of drinks with prices and blinking select lights, ¥130 display, coin slot, PUSH tray), the thermos pot with its pump button, water gauge, 98° display, keep-warm lamp, steam and a mug under the spout, and a mint fridge covered in notes with Tama's photo on it. Below: the drinks redrawn to match.

Round 3, the dispense, slowed down (read left to right, top to bottom): the can clunks into the tray and the flap swings up; the pot's pump goes down and pours into the mug; the fridge door swings open in a puff of cold, then shuts.
Round 3, in the game at 1366x860: the first command. Lights dip, the can drops into the tray, the flap opens and the cola flies to Kenji.
Round 3, phone 390x844, shift 3: all three machines, a little bigger than before.
Round 3, desktop 1366x860, shift 1.
Round 3, desktop 1366x860, shift 3.
Fix, phone 390: the title now says the goal in one line, with the dots drawn.
Fix, the first minute, step 1 of 3: a hand on Kenji, the step card says "Tap Kenji, then に (to)". Kenji asks politely: コーラを ください！ Other taps wait until the hand's one is done.
Step 2 of 3: Kenji has に, the hand moves to the cola: "Tap the cola, then を (what)".
Step 3 of 3: "Press だして". The whole English translation sits on its own line under the tiles and wraps instead of being cut off.
After the walkthrough: Mio, in です/ます: つぎは わたしです / コーヒー、いいですか？ The goal and the commands left stay under the top bar.
Shift 2: と is taught the first time it matters, with the hand on each tap (Kenji, と, Mori, に, coffee を).
Phone 360x780, shift 3: four people, three machines, every line whole.
Desktop at your window size (1000x645): on a short window the talk sits beside the sentence, so the room and the full translation both fit.
Desktop 1000x645: the と step.
Desktop 1000x645: the power word pick between shifts.
Desktop 1000x645: the end card.
Desktop 1920x1080: step 2 of the walkthrough.

Frame strip, phone: the first と combo in shift 2. ケンジくんと モリさんに コーヒーを だしてください: the lights dip, the command rises off the vending machine, two cans fly, both bubbles pop, then 2 × 2 with the streak and ください multipliers.
Frame strip, phone: the particles swapped on purpose. コーヒーに ミオさんを だして puts Mio out of the vending machine and lands her on the coffee, then one line says what を and に said.

options.label: kotodama: fun, keep going with it
options.note: The pitch: B2 after six, and the old machines do exactly what Eric says, word for word. You build each command from the room itself (tap who and what, give each a particle, then fire the verb), and the particles decide what flies where. Requests pile up faster than one command can answer them one at a time, so と (two or three people served in one sentence) is the combo you need, scored 2 × 2 or 3 × 3 with a streak on top. Between shifts you pick a power word: も, みんな, まって or ください. Three shifts, three hearts, a daily run with a best score. The design page, with what it borrows and an honest check, is game3d/minigames/README.md (Kotodama). The screens come from a headless run of the daily seed; the frame strips are from game3d/minigames/tools/frames.mjs.
